==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|re-view||rare for noun|obsolete for verb}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|revewe}}, {{m|enm|reveue}}, from {{der|en|fro|reveue|reveüe}}, {{m|fro|revue}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|revue}}), feminine form of {{m|fro|reveu|reveü}}, past participle of {{m|fro|reveoir}} (French: {{m|fr|revoir}}), from {{der|en|la|revideō}}, from {{m|la|re-}} +{{m|la|videō||see, observe}} (English: {{m|en|video}}). Equivalent to {{prefix|en|re|view}}. Compare {{m|en|retrospect}}. {{doublet|en|revue}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# A second or [[subsequent]] [[reading]] of a text or artifact in an attempt to gain new insights.
#: {{ux|en|I need to make a '''review''' of the book before I can understand it.}}
# An [[account]] intended as a critical [[evaluation]] of a text or a piece of work.
#: {{ux|en|The newspaper '''review''' was full of praise for the play.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1971|author=Peter Brown|title=The World of Late Antiquity: AD 150—750|page=54|publisher=Thames & Hudson LTD|year_published=2013|isbn=0393958035
|passage=The more strongly people felt about their ideas, the more potent the demons seemed to them: Christians believed that traditional paganism, far from being the work of men, was an 'opium of the masses', pumped into the human race by the non-human demons; and one scholar even ascribed bad '''reviews''' of his book to demonic inspiration!}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} A judicial [[reassessment]] of a case or an event.
#: {{ux|en|The victims demanded a full judicial '''review''' of the case.}}
# A [[stage]] [[show]] made up of [[topical]] [[sketch]]es etc.
#: {{syn|en|revue}}
#: {{ux|en|The Cambridge Footlights '''Review''' launched many Monty Python faces.}}
# A [[survey]] of the available items or material.
#: {{ux|en|The magazine contained a '''review''' of Paris restaurants.}}
# {{lb|en|science}} A [[review article]].
# A [[periodical]] which makes a [[survey]] of the arts or some other field.
#: {{ux|en|The Times Literary '''Review''' is published in London.}}
# A military [[inspection]] or [[display]] for the benefit of superiors or VIPs.
#: {{ux|en|The troops assembled for a '''review''' by the Queen.}}
# A forensic [[inspection]] to assess [[compliance]] with regulations or some code.
#: {{ux|en|The regulators demanded a '''review''' against NYSE practices.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|to survey}} To [[survey]]; to look broadly over.
#: {{ux|en|Before I tackle the question directly, I must briefly '''review''' historical approaches to the problem.}}
# To write a critical evaluation of a new art work etc.; to write a review.
#: {{ux|en|The critic '''reviews''' every new play in London.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=w:David E. Sanger|title=Countering cyberattacks without a playbook [print version: A cyberwar with no playbook, ''International New York Times'', 26 December 2014, p. 18]|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2014/12/24/world/asia/countering-cyberattacks-without-a-playbook.html|date=23 December 2014|passage={{...}} "[[w:The Interview (2014 film)|The Interview]]," a crude and poorly '''reviewed''' comedy about a C.I.A. effort to hire two bumbling journalists to knock off {{w|Kim Jong-un}}, the {{w|North Korea}}n leader {{...}}|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250702085343/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/12/24/world/asia/countering-cyberattacks-without-a-playbook.html|archivedate=2 July 2025}}
# To look back over in order to [[correct]] or [[edit]]; to [[revise]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|Philippines|sometimes|North America}} To [[look over]] [[again]] (something previously written or learned), especially in [[preparation]] for an [[examination]].
#: {{syn|en|revise<q:UK, Australia, New Zealand>}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To view or see again; to look back on.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|IV|iv|text=''Cam''[''illo'']   What I do next, ſhall be next to tell the King // Of this Eſcape, and whither they are bound: // Wherein my hope is, I ſhall ſo prevail, // To force him after: in whoſe company // I ſhall '''review''' ''Sicilia''; for whoſe ſight, // I have a Woman’s Longing.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To retrace; to go over again.
#* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|volume=I|book=III|lines=127–128|page=100|text=Shall I the long, laborious ſcene '''review''', // And open all the wounds of ''Greece'' anew?}}
